audit.selector: The source fixes F(T,p) at the original tree and rank. No argument in the reviewed route changes F after a move or collapses equal-support leaves.

clone_identity.upper: For fixed v in F, an independent A in H_v of size p meeting W_v maps to B=A union {v}; conversely a B clone tagged v has v in B and B\{v} independent, avoids s_v, and meets W_v, so recovers A. The same bijection holds at size p-1 for lower clones.
clone_identity.count: For each r, tagged clone occurrences at size r+1 are sum_v [i_r(H_v)-i_r(R_v)]. Subtracting ranks p and p-1 gives S(T,p), including distinct tags for shared supports.
clone_identity.edge_projection: Under the source report's stated old operations (delete retaining the tag; retag while deleting the old tagged leaf), the underlying set pair is a one-vertex deletion. Thus it is admitted by the new complete clone fiber over deletion pairs.

guard_arithmetic_from_reported_switch_ro.finding: The displayed numbers satisfy both guards, but no adjacency list or exact ordinary-tree encoding is provided, so the asserted row and switch were not reproducible here.

flow_audit.values_checked_against_copied_common_ins: state counts, transport arc counts, upper supply, lower capacity, flow, saturation, and zero cut deficit match the route report
flow_audit.limitation: No per-case primal/cut artifacts were present among the case-listed files; the flow figures were not independently replayed. The code's bounded outputs do not prove universal Hall or the aggregate.

audit.scope_fence: The matching assertion is stronger than S(T,p)<=0. A failed matching or Hall cut would not refute S(T,p)<=0; successful flows on three trees do not establish universal matching.
